title: Customer routing contracts & snapshot PRD sketch
summary: A lightweight PRD sketch proposing a small 'routing contract' between Redwood control plane and customer-managed network agents plus a compact snapshot artifact that serves both audit and fast rollback needs. Goal = minimal customer friction for VPC handoff + strong forensic trail without a large storage bill.
background: Current private deploy notes focus a lot on approval flow and large attestation bundles. We keep hearing from customers and SRE that the heavy evidence packages are friction at onboarding time and slow down incident triage. Also some customers want the ability to snapshot routing state at a point-in-time and ship a compact proof to the control plane for later verification. This doc experiments with a contract + snapshot format and UX for operator flows.
goals:
- Define a compact routing contract (what routes are managed, which prefixes are allowed to change, handshake semantics)
- Define a small snapshot artifact (~<5KB index + optional compressed delta) with signed metadata for audit/rollback
- Surface operator UX for handoff, quick rollback, and incident evidence retrieval
- Keep storage and export costs predictable (configurable TTL, sampling)
non_goals:
- This is not a full attestation system for every packet/path. Not building complex PKI or notarization here.
- Not replacing existing SIEM integrations; export hooks suffice.
assumptions: Customers run a lightweight agent or provide a signed manifest from their network admin
Control plane can store small blobs and index them per-customer with retention policies
Customers accept an initial quick onboarding handshake that confirms policy constraints
Operators need both fast rollback and concise forensic evidence (not verbose PCAPs)
user_stories: As an operator, I want to snap a compact routing snapshot before a risky change so I can roll back reliably.
As a security auditor, I want a verifiable digest of the network policy at deploy-time so I can confirm compliance without reading large logs.
As a support engineer, I want a short provenance file to triage incidents quickly and hand to the customer.
proposed_design:
High-level sketch:

1) Routing Contract (JSON contract)
- contract_id: uuid
- managed_prefixes: list of CIDRs the control plane may program or request changes for
- immutable_prefixes: CIDRs customer won't allow overrides
- allowed_peers: optional list of peer-ids (for cross-account peering)
- change_window_policy: e.g., allow immediate / require 15m approval / scheduled
- signing_key_meta: key id and fingerprint used by customer to sign snapshots

2) Snapshot Artifact (compact, signed)
- snapshot_id, contract_id, created_at, sequence_no
- route_digest: Merkle-ish digest of route table entries (compact hash array)
- config_checksums: hashes of iptables / route-maps / BGP conf snippets used to generate the snapshot
- minimal evidence: small list of observed route announcements and the control-plane decision refs (token refs to detailed logs kept only if retention enabled)
- signature: customer-signed blob (support either agent-signed JWT or HSM-signed envelope)

3) Handshake/Flows
- onboarding: customer uploads routing contract and pubkey; Redwood returns contract_id and a psuedo-challenge; customer agent signs challenge and control plane stores contract with 'pending' until validated by SRE or automated checks
- pre-change snapshot: operator triggers snapshot via agent or API; snapshot uploaded and verified by control plane; if verification passes, change proceeds; snapshot stored for TTL (default 90 days) and searchable by snapshot_id
- rollback: control plane can request agent to apply snapshot or provide rollback instructions to customer operator. For fully-managed Dedicated customers, Redwood can push rollback with explicit allow flag on contract.
audit_and_telemetry:
- Each snapshot yields a small audit record: snapshot_id, contract_id, user, action (create/change/rollback), size, retention_ttl.
- Sampling: by default store full audit index; large evidence logs (pcap/flow dumps) are referenced by token and only kept if customer enables retention.
- Query interface: per-customer snapshot timeline, fingerprint search, time-based restore hints.
- Alerts: if snapshot signing fails, generate high-severity alarm for SRE and customer.
- Cost controls: cap snapshot frequency per contract (e.g., 10/day) and provide burst purchase options.
ops_playbook:
- Onboarding checks: validate contract schema, confirm key fingerprint over Slack/Zoom, run small simulated snapshot test.
- Incident triage: fetch latest snapshot, compute diff against current desired state, surface candidate rollback steps.
- Escalation: if signature mismatch or missing evidence, route to security oncall; if agent unreachable, mark snapshot as 'stale' and include operator note.
- Retention admin: product UI to set default TTL per customer and per-contract overrides.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: API sketch + internal agent prototype (2 sprints)
Phase 1: Beta with 3 existing Dedicated customers (manual onboarding SRE-assisted)
Phase 2: Add UI controls, TTL settings, and sampling knobs; expand to Private customers with self-serve onboarding
Phase 3: Integrate with Optimize and Console for snapshot cost suggestions and automated rollback policies.
Rollout metrics: onboarding time, snapshot frequency, snapshots per incident, storage cost per customer.
open_questions: Encryption model: do we accept agent-signed JWTs or require HSM-backed signatures?
What is the minimum snapshot granularity that still supports reliable rollback? (routes only vs routes+policy)
Retention defaults: 30/90/365 days — what are legal/regulatory expectations in EU vs US?
Do we allow Redwood to perform automatic rollback for Dedicated customers, or always require customer approval?
todo: Prototype route_digest format and test collision properties
Write a minimal contract JSON schema and publish to Confluence

notes_to_self: Keep the snapshot small. If it grows >5KB on average we'll need a different export model. Focus on digest+checksums + token references to verbose logs. Be explicit about 'control plane only indexes' vs 'retriable evidence kept by customer.'
